# link

> Develop, test and communicate intrinsic habitat and connectivity
> models for the BC Freshwater Atlas stream network

link is a tool for building models of where each fish species could
spawn and rear on a stream network, and which of that habitat fish can
reach. Current models rate habitat from stream gradient, channel width
and discharge, resolve access past natural barriers such as falls and
steep gradients, and record the road and rail crossings and dams that
sit below. Its value is flexibility: every rule and threshold is a row
in a config, so a model can be changed, run beside another, checked
against fish observations and traced back to the rules that produced it.

![Map of the Parsnip River watershed group with stream reaches coloured
by Arctic grayling spawning, rearing and access, and by the barrier type
below each reach](reference/figures/readme-pars.png)

*Arctic grayling habitat in the Parsnip River watershed group. Purple
reaches drain to Williston Reservoir behind the W.A.C. Bennett Dam.
Orange and red reaches sit above a road or rail crossing that is a
barrier. Grey reaches lie above a natural barrier to grayling.*

## Installation

``` r

pak::pak("NewGraphEnvironment/link")
```

link is under active development and its functions change between
releases (see
[NEWS](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/link/news/index.html)). Pin
a release for reproducible work:
`pak::pak("NewGraphEnvironment/link@vX.Y.Z")`.

link runs against a PostgreSQL database holding the BC Freshwater Atlas
through [fwapg](https://github.com/smnorris/fwapg), set up as for
[fresh](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/fresh).

## Example

A model is a config, and its rules are tables you can read and edit:

``` r

library(link)

cfg    <- lnk_config("default")
loaded <- lnk_load_overrides(cfg)

th <- loaded$parameters_habitat_thresholds
th[th$species_code %in% c("BT", "GR"),
   c("species_code", "spawn_gradient_max", "spawn_channel_width_min",
     "rear_gradient_max", "rear_channel_width_min")]
#>   species_code spawn_gradient_max spawn_channel_width_min rear_gradient_max rear_channel_width_min
#> 1           BT             0.0549                       2            0.1049                    1.5
#> 2           GR             0.0249                       4            0.0349                    1.5
```

Run it for a watershed group, then sum the habitat each species can
reach:

``` r

conn <- lnk_db_conn()
cfg$pipeline$schema <- "fresh_default"
lnk_pipeline_run(conn, aoi = "PARS", cfg = cfg, loaded = loaded,
                 mapping_code = TRUE)

lnk_rollup_wsg(conn, aoi = "PARS", species = c("BT", "GR"),
               schema = "fresh_default")
#>    wsg species accessible_km spawning_km rearing_km rearing_lake_connection_km
#> 1 PARS      BT       6883.03     1685.38    2635.01                          0
#> 2 PARS      GR       4442.31      983.86    1366.32                          0
```

Change a threshold, run again, and compare. Each run records its inputs,
its parameters and the source versions its data was loaded from, in log
tables beside its results.

  a full run for one watershed group, with maps for both species.

## Ecosystem

| Package | Role |
|----|----|
| **link** | Intrinsic habitat models: develop, test and communicate (this package) |
| [fresh](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/fresh) | Stream network modelling engine: segment, classify, cluster, aggregate |
| [wet](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/wet) | Stream flow and water temperature for BC’s Freshwater Atlas |
| [gq](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/gq) | Shared map symbology |

## Data and methods it builds on

link’s access model follows the method of
[bcfishpass](https://github.com/smnorris/bcfishpass), built by Simon
Norris and maintained with contributions from many groups. link also
reads bcfishpass’s community-maintained corrections to crossings,
barriers and habitat, synced weekly into the `default` and `bcfishpass`
configs so they stay in one place. A `bcfishpass` config applies
bcfishpass’s own rules, so results can be checked against the method
they come from. Fish observations come from
[bcfishobs](https://github.com/smnorris/bcfishobs), and the stream
network from [fwapg](https://github.com/smnorris/fwapg) and the [BC
Freshwater
Atlas](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/data/geographic-data-services/topographic-data/freshwater).

## Citation

``` r

citation("link")
```

# Package index

## All functions

- [`lnk_access()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/link/reference/lnk_access.md)
  : Build per-segment per-species access from schema tables (portable)

- [`lnk_aggregate()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/link/reference/lnk_aggregate.md)
  : Compute upstream habitat per crossing

- [`lnk_artifact_probe()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/link/reference/lnk_artifact_probe.md)
  : Probe the FWA primitives' artifacts and record what is current now

- [`lnk_artifact_read()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/link/reference/lnk_artifact_read.md)
  : Read the recorded source artifacts, one row per expected artifact

- [`lnk_artifact_record()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/link/reference/lnk_artifact_record.md)
  : Record source-artifact identity for DB primitives

- [`lnk_barrier_overrides()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/link/reference/lnk_barrier_overrides.md)
  : Build barrier override list from evidence sources

- [`lnk_barriers_emit()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/link/reference/lnk_barriers_emit.md)
  : Emit slim crossings_lookup + per-source barriers\_\* tables

- [`lnk_barriers_unify()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/link/reference/lnk_barriers_unify.md)
  :

  Unify per-WSG barrier sources into the working-schema
  `<schema>.barriers`

- [`lnk_barriers_views()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/link/reference/lnk_barriers_views.md)
  :

  Create working-schema views over `<persist_schema>.barriers`

- [`lnk_baseline_append()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/link/reference/lnk_baseline_append.md)
  : Append a row to the run-tracking baseline ledger

- [`lnk_baseline_current()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/link/reference/lnk_baseline_current.md)
  : Is this host's baseline already current at the supplied upstream?

- [`lnk_baseline_read()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/link/reference/lnk_baseline_read.md)
  : Read the run-tracking baseline ledger

- [`lnk_bucket_get()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/link/reference/lnk_bucket_get.md)
  : Download a single artifact from a public S3 bucket prefix

- [`lnk_bucket_log()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/link/reference/lnk_bucket_log.md)
  :

  Read the build-identifier `log.json` from a bucket prefix

- [`lnk_catalog()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/link/reference/lnk_catalog.md)
  : Read a habitat export's manifest

- [`lnk_compare_mapping_code()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/link/reference/lnk_compare_mapping_code.md)
  : Compare one watershed group's persisted mapping_code tokens against
  a reference

- [`lnk_compare_rollup()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/link/reference/lnk_compare_rollup.md)
  : Compare one watershed group's persisted state against a reference

- [`lnk_compare_wsg()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/link/reference/lnk_compare_wsg.md)
  : Compare one watershed group against a reference dataset

- [`lnk_config()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/link/reference/lnk_config.md)
  : Load a Pipeline Config Bundle (Manifest)

- [`lnk_config_verify()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/link/reference/lnk_config_verify.md)
  : Verify Config Bundle File Checksums and Shape

- [`lnk_db_conn()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/link/reference/lnk_db_conn.md)
  : Connect to FWA PostgreSQL database

  : Load a habitat export into PostgreSQL

- [`lnk_fanout_judge()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/link/reference/lnk_fanout_judge.md)
  : Judge the outcome of a parallel fan-out

- [`lnk_habitat_gate()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/link/reference/lnk_habitat_gate.md)

  : Score the habitat one threshold step adds or removes

  : Verify that required Postgres tables exist in a connection

  : Load override CSVs into a database table

- [`lnk_override()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/link/reference/lnk_override.md)
  : Validate and apply overrides to a table

  : Initialize persistent province-wide habitat tables
